[docs/providers.md#onprem-on-premises]
A queue, bucket or topic can live in a service you already run: declare it under [`resources:`](resources.md) with `options.driver`. Queues take `directory` or `redis`, storage takes `directory` or `s3` (MinIO and other S3-compatible stores), and topics take `directory`. `pskit dashboard --serve` shows the host's health, stats, logs and workflow executions.

[docs/events.md#http]
**Path templates** pskit's runtime also matches routes itself, so path params and `405 Method Not Allowed` work the same on clouds with no API gateway (GCP, IBM, DigitalOcean, Cloudflare), including when the platform adds or strips a path prefix. Two functions may not declare the same `METHOD /path`.

[docs/events.md#queue]
On premises the same options are implemented by a file broker (`batch_size`, `batch_window`, visibility, dead-letter, `max_receive`, `fifo`). `BatchResult` retries only the failed message ids, as on AWS. Set `provider.options.services.queue` to `builtin` (created at start) or `{use: directory, path: ...}`. `existing: true` waits for that directory. Example: [`examples/04-queue-worker`](../examples/04-queue-worker) and [`examples/16-on-premises`](../examples/16-on-premises).

[docs/events.md#schedule]
The handler gets `event.type == "schedule"` and `event.data == input`. pskit converts the portable syntax to each cloud's dialect: A rate that can't be expressed as cron on cron-only clouds (e.g. `7 minutes`) fails validation; use a divisor of 60 minutes or 24 hours. `timezone` is honoured by AWS, GCP and Alibaba (cron form); Azure ignores it with a warning.

[docs/events.md#events-backed-by-a-resource]
The event uses the resource's native name and `existing: <external>`. The functions also get the resource's connection details. On premises, a resource can move the queue to Redis or the bucket to an S3-compatible store, and a storage event may set both `resource` and `bucket`: that bucket on the resource's storage service ([details](resources.md#storage-drivers)).

[docs/events.md#events-triggers]
`smtp` (on premises) runs a function when mail arrives for your domain: `- smtp: {resource: inbound-mail}` on the SMTP server created under *On-prem services* (an `smtp` resource). The handler gets from, to, cc, subject, text, html, headers and attachments, plus the same mail as an Amazon SES event (`Records[0].ses`). Setup and DNS records: [smtp/README.md](smtp/README.md).
